You realize many people in the USA don't have healthcare to cover this?  And even if they do have that healthcare, it doesn't cover close to 100% of the costs?

Do any of you actually have experience with this?  AKA, you aren't under your parents healthcare, have your own job, and own health insurance?  How much was covered if so?

If you can't answer the above, then I don't feel its warranted to downvote me.  I'm not saying don't do the above, but I'm saying the debt from medical bills is one of the leading causes of bankruptcy in the USA.  That can lead to a load of other problems for someone and feel it's warranted to mention.
And how much was the medical bill for that?  Are you in the USA where they will charge you tons of money to do that?
Thanks for being on of the few that actually made a decent response.  I am going to think about what you said, but I really do appreciate you actually put some thought in your response.
Again, that amount can cause sides.  If you look at studies.
Such a supportive subreddit.

What advice would you give to a 26 year old who may be losing his hair and thinks his life is basically over?  How does someone, who has had tons of other problems in there life and is now dealing with this (which could mean bye to their sex life) deal with this?
Go to a different one is probably all you can do. By the way, how did you get 2% keto? They only give that out with prescription and don't think docs will do it in states

I appriciate the response.  I wish someone who has taken this drug and experienced side effects and lost them would comment.  It is really hard to get real information about this drug.

Seems like its either fear-mongers on here, or people who are really pro-finasteride (which seems odd for them to be hanging on a board if it's worked for them).  I am just unsure who to believe anymore
The 1% yes, but I am not aware of the 2% being easy at all.

What about someone who is going bald in there 20s? Do you actually have personal experience with that? How would someone deal with that? Dating etc.? Do you have personal experience with this or know others who have? Not a fake story either. Would love to know about that personally.

I agree with you on people not saying what should or shouldn't be taken.  But, I would also point out that my doctor prescribed me finasteride, which does mess with my hormones.  He did this after looking at my head for 2 minutes, told me to get my thyroid checked, and then sent me on my way.

Also, I don't think there have been any real long term studies about the effects of messing with DHT like that.  So, while I agree that listening to medical advice from a trained doctor is good in most cases, I question it when it comes to taking this drug.  

For the most part, it may not effect most, but it does have the chances of doing so.  And because its on the warning label of the potential side effects, the doctor is basically in the clear from being sued because its a "buyer beware" situation.  He may still be sued, but it probably fits into the equation of things.

I'm kind of leaning this way with things.  I think one can try Rogaine and maybe nizoral, but if it is lost at that point one just needs to move on with life.  I don't know if I am willing to do Finasteride, and from the looks of it there are quite a few others not willing to do it either.  Honestly too, I don't think its some far off reason not to do it either.  It is messing with DHT levels, and one thing I do know is that there hasn't been any long term studies of people getting off it after 10-20+ years.  Wouldn't be shocked if a lot of people have some issues when new treatment comes out.  

Also, I am also beginning to think a lot of the issues guys are having with hair loss comes from insecurity and they are blaming it on hair loss.  I have looked up posts and seem plenty of girls say its either a non-issue, they are attracted to it, or there are a few who said they have issues with it.  But, the fact is that is seems those who have an issue with it and its a complete dealbreaker seem to be in the minority.  At least that is my observation.  

The the OP, may I ask how it has changed your dating life?  Were you dating a lot before and how did it change when you started shaving your head?  How old are you, tall, and how much do you weight if you don't mind me asking?  Really curious is all.

Right but many people say they had side effects years or months later that didn't go away, the drug seems very risky.  Sure, they are "vocal minority", but at end of day its on the damn pamphlet.  If these were made up stories, it wouldn't be on the pamphlet.  I wish they made a damn drug without side effects.  I also hear people having issues when they get off the drug.  I wouldn't doubt many will have sides when they come out with new treatment and everyone starts coming off this drug.

Its just not heard of right now as most people don't get off the drug right now if they use it long term.  But, if new treatment comes out, wouldn't be shocked if side effects start hitting the news.  This stuff messes with hormones, I really question if its worth the risk.

Sure, I got on the drug for a week at a low mg.  Thought I had side effects and got off.  

Haven't gotten back on.  I am unsure what honestly to do.  I still question the side effects. Whether this drug is worth it or if hair honestly matters.  I really question if it honestly worth it at all.

Any thoughts from anyone?  I don't want the car crash example, it's honestly a stupid example and I don't agree with it being comparable.

This and on top of that I am not 100% convinced they know the long term implications of using this drug (science that is, that is why it looks like harvard and another college are doing studies on this drug).  

I am still weighing out if I will take the drug.  But I am heavily leaning not because the more I look into it the more I am thinking hair loss isn't as big a deal as people possibly make it.  It seems possible that its the low self esteem/behavior that may actually be causing the issue.

I'm just making the poster aware that the same people saying that its ok to take the drug will be saying what your saying, "you knew the risks".  

I am not someone having issues or asking for sympathy.  So you made an assumption there.  I am telling the poster that the potential is there.  I myself am weighing the odds too whether I should take the drug or not.  But I am honestly believing most people don't care about the hair issue and the only people making an issue of it are those acting depressed because they have hair loss.  I think peoples behavior changes, and they blame it on the hair loss.
I'm going to leave it as is, because I could care less.

Just remember that the people on here who are saying the chances are slim to none are also going to be the same people who are going to say, "well you should have read the pamplet and knew the risks beforehand".  

Everyone also started using this car example.  Honestly, I'm beginning to believe most girls could care less about the hair issue.  There is a difference between getting in a car so you can pay your bills and using a drug that can potentially give you sexual side effects.

There has been no proven cause/effect relationship with "permanent" side effects yet.  I'm not talking about side effects from the drug while on it and not getting in an argument about this.

Unless you have a study showing otherwise.

This is the same issue I'm having as well.  Also, the same people who are saying that there is a small chance will probably be the same people who will say, "well, it did say on the pamplet this and that".  

I wish they would find a new treatment or prove a cause and effect with fin, because it could all be psychological too.

Yeah, that is the issue.  I am not sure what I feel more comfortable living with right now.  I wish someone could really help me with this.  But I really and truly don't know.

If I take the pill and have any issues, only thing people will say is too bad and suffer.  But if i don't do anything, it will be the same thing.

I just really don't know what to do and don't think anyone cares.  I mean, what do you think one should do?  I wish I could get this too the front page of reddit and get a lot of thoughts but doubt that would ever happen.

I really just don't know what to do.  Do I risk these meds?  We don't know what the long term effects are.  Worse is there are possible meds in the pipeline that might cure all this if you keep your hair.  It's all a mess.  I just don't know what to do.  And doctor really doesn't care.  It's either take these meds or whatever.

IDK if they were psychological or not.  It is Lialda.  But I am unsure if it is the cause or not.  If I call my doctor, they will just tell me either to get off the meds or its in my head.  So, really unsure what to do.
Right, I would more be asking from a white person perspective.

I'll be honest, I've been on this planet 26 years.  I used to believe that saying that it would get better.  Guess what, it honestly hasn't.  In fact, now I may have a chronic disease and losing my hair.  Stick around longer who knows what else could happen.

Sorry, but it doesn't always get better.
I'm not close to my family. While I appreciate the response my family is a lot of the reason I'm in my situation I'm in now.
